newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares fall 1.05 pct on liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares fall 1.05 pct on liquidity squeeze.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted losses on Thursday in thin trade caused by a continuing lack of liquidity due to ongoing political uneasiness and an approaching holiday, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,514, down 16 points, or 1.05 percent from Wednesday, but up slightly from a late low of 1,500. Volume dropped to 17.49 trillion lira from Wednesday's 21.12 trillion.
"The market turned downward because of liquidity shortage. Political uncertainties hinder cash influx to the market," said Mursel Yildiz from Vakifbank securities.
Several brokers expect support at around the index's 1,500 level to hold.

Reluctance to buy ahead of an upcoming long holiday and recent share offers by new firms have also caused a cash drain from the market, brokers said. A bank and a commercial vehicle venture floated part of their capital last week and a private hospital is offering part of its capital to the public this week.

A religious holiday between April 17-21 will be followed by an official holiday on April 23. The government has declared April 22 a holiday for state offices, but it is not yet known if the markets will be closed.

Of the 243 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 151 to 45 and 47 were stable. The IMKB Industrial lost 0.98 percent to 1,515, the IMKB Services dived 2.47 percent to 1,420 and the IMKB Financial eased 0.8 percent to 1,615.

Actives were led by largely state owned flat steel maker Eregli, down 750 lira at 15,500 and ground handling firm Celebi Hava Servisi, steady at 75,000 lira. They made up 11 percent of the total turnover.
